description: Eight-panel composite of field-emission SEM micrographs showing the microstructure of an Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel plate in different states; all panels are secondary-electron images, no numeric data are plotted. (a) HR (hot-rolled), 50 µm scale bar: strongly laminated structure of elongated δ-ferrite (δ-F) bands alternating with lath martensite (M), with small arrowed retained austenite (RA) inside the martensite bands. (b) HR, 10 µm scale bar: higher-magnification view with α-ferrite (α-F), M and δ-F arrowed separately. (c) IQ-1050, 50 µm: the laminated banding persists. (d) IQ-1050, 10 µm: thinner, discontinuous δ-F grains outlined by arrows, prior austenite grain boundaries (PAGB) arrowed, larger M region. (e)–(h) QA (quenched-annealed) tempered martensite at 620, 680, 740 and 800 °C, each with a 5 µm scale bar: fine reverted austenite (A) among martensitic laths; (e) contains a yellow-boxed inset (1 µm scale bar) showing widely distributed carbides (Cm); (h) has a red dashed box marking new martensite formed from austenite on air cooling. Together the panels document the evolution of the banded δ-ferrite/martensite structure and of austenite reversion with annealing temperature. Scale bars 1, 5, 10 and 50 µm.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (b) are SEM micrographs of the hot-rolled (HR) state with 50 µm and 10 µm scale bars respectively; both show elongated δ-ferrite (δ-F) bands alternating with lath martensite (M).
Small arrowed retained austenite (RA) particles are visible inside the martensite bands in (a) and (c).
Panel (b) additionally labels α-ferrite (α-F) separately from δ-ferrite (δ-F) and martensite (M).
In (d) the δ-ferrite appears as thin, discontinuous grains and arrows labelled PAGB point to prior austenite grain boundaries crossing the martensite.
Panel (e) contains an inset with a 1 µm scale bar in which finely distributed carbides labelled Cm are visible within tempered martensite; the main field of (e) has a 5 µm scale bar.
Panels (f)–(h) share the same 5 µm scale bar and show progressively coarser lath martensite with reverted austenite (A) arrowed among the laths.
Panel (h) (QA-800) contains a red dashed rectangle highlighting a region identified in the caption as new martensite formed from austenite during air cooling.
The caption states that M = martensite, RA = retained austenite, δ-F = δ ferrite, α-F = α ferrite, PAGB = prior austenitic grain boundary, A = austenite and Cm = carbides.

The citing text states that the hot-rolled condition shows a laminated microstructure of δ-ferrite bands and lath martensite formed by thermomechanical rolling in the dual-phase region, with α-ferrite and lath martensite forming on cooling.

The citing text states that the laminated microstructure still exists in IO-1050 owing to heredity, but that prior austenite grain growth at 1050 °C thinned and even broke the δ-ferrite bands into discontinuous grains.

The citing text attributes the larger martensite fraction and lower retained austenite in IQ-1050 to reduced Mn in reversed austenite, lowered austenite stability, higher Ms and the faster water-quenching rate.
The citing text states that cementite carbides (Cm) precipitated only at an annealing temperature of 620 °C, as shown in panel (e).

The citing text states that fine reverted austenite grains were observed among tempered martensitic laths at all four annealing temperatures and that new martensite existed in the tempered martensite region of QA-800 (red box in panel (h)).
No numeric property values, axis scales or composition tables are printed anywhere in the figure; the only numeric labels are the scale bars (1, 5, 10 and 50 µm) and the specimen codes.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of the hot-rolled (HR) state with a 50 µm scale bar; a laminated (banded) structure of elongated δ-ferrite (δ-F) bands alternating with lath martensite (M); small retained austenite (RA) regions arrowed inside the martensite bands.
SEM micrograph of the HR state at higher magnification, 10 µm scale bar; arrowed labels α-F (α-ferrite), M (lath martensite) and δ-F (dark δ-ferrite band running across the lower part of the field).
SEM micrograph of IQ-1050 with a 50 µm scale bar; the laminated δ-ferrite/martensite banding is still present, with δ-F, M and RA arrowed.

SEM micrograph of IQ-1050 at higher magnification, 10 µm scale bar; δ-ferrite appears as thinner, discontinuous grains with arrows, prior austenite grain boundaries (PAGB) are arrowed, and a large lath martensite (M) region fills the field.
SEM micrograph of QA-620 (5 µm scale bar) showing tempered martensite with fine reverted austenite (A); a yellow-boxed inset with a 1 µm scale bar shows widely distributed fine carbides labelled Cm.

SEM micrograph of QA-680 (5 µm scale bar) showing a coarser lath/lamellar tempered-martensite structure with reverted austenite (A) arrowed; a yellow-boxed inset with a 1 µm scale bar gives a magnified view of the laths.
SEM micrograph of QA-740 (5 µm scale bar) showing lath martensite with reverted austenite (A) arrowed between the laths.
SEM micrograph of QA-800 (5 µm scale bar) labelled δ-F, M and A, with a red dashed box on the right marking a region of new martensite formed from austenite during air cooling.
